items.title: How Dream Racers uses Roblox's Cube AI to generate playable vehicles in real time
items.excerpt: A new Roblox game, Dream Racers, integrates generative AI directly into gameplay by letting players build and race unique karts. It is one of the first shipped titles to put Roblox's Cube 3D generation model into a live player-facing loop.
items.why: Generative 3D stops being a pre-production asset trick and becomes a runtime design material — the player prompts, the game has to keep it playable.

items.title: Nimble Fox launches AI tool for building Unity games worldwide
items.excerpt: A Helsinki startup is releasing an AI copilot built into the Unity editor on Sept. 7, letting developers build and modify games by prompting inside the engine. Rather than generating a whole game in one pass, it works feature by feature — mechanics, UI flows, scoped changes — reading the context of an existing project.
items.why: In-editor, project-aware, feature-at-a-time prompting is the shape AI game tooling is settling into — closer to a collaborator in the scene than a text-to-game button.

items.title: Nvidia's DLSS 5 looks compelling in NBA 2K with performance improvements since March — but will gamers accept it?
items.excerpt: Nvidia showed its latest progress with DLSS 5 for enhancing 3D images in games, demonstrating photorealistic content in NBA 2K27 with substantial gains since the March reveal.
items.why: A neural layer that rewrites the final frame moves art direction downstream of the artist — the open question is whether players read it as fidelity or as filter.

items.title: Nvidia says DLSS 5 comes with a 50-60% performance hit, which makes me wonder what we're doing here
items.excerpt: Nvidia has confirmed DLSS 5's 3D-guided neural rendering costs 50-60% of frame rate on average, inverting the original promise of DLSS as a performance technology.
items.why: The cost model flips: AI rendering is now a look you pay for in frames, which turns it into an explicit art-direction budget decision rather than free uplift.

items.title: Nvidia snuck me into a room to show off DLSS 5 in person, and it's somehow beautiful, ugly, impressive, and troubling all at the same time
items.excerpt: A hands-on account of Nvidia's private DLSS 5 demo, where the neural rendering pass produces images that are simultaneously more lifelike and less like the game the artists built.
items.why: First-hand craft critique of what a generative render pass actually does to authored visual style — the exact tension designers will have to arbitrate.

items.title: Dwarf Fortress creator says we have a natural lean towards human-made stories, 'but we're all going to be very sorely tested in the coming years' by AI
items.excerpt: Tarn Adams, whose game is built almost entirely on procedural generation, argues players instinctively prefer human-authored stories but that the preference will be severely tested as generative systems improve.
items.why: The most credible proceduralist in games drawing the line between generated systems and generated authorship — a working distinction for anyone designing with AI.

items.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 lead says Nvidia DLSS 5 backlash is "really funny," and that "most talented people I know" use AI
items.excerpt: A KCD2 lead pushes back on the DLSS 5 backlash, arguing that the most capable developers he knows already use AI tools in their day-to-day work.
items.why: A shipping AAA lead putting a number on how normalized AI already is inside craft teams, against the public-facing backlash.

items.title: Nvidia DLSS 5 is launching on September 3: Here's everything I learned about it from a private Gamescom demo
items.excerpt: A reporter shut in a room with four Nvidia engineers gets into the mechanics of DLSS 5 — how the neural pass is guided by 3D data, what developers have to do to support it, and where it breaks.
items.why: The engineering detail matters for pipelines: it defines what art teams must hand the model and how much control they keep.

items.title: 30 years later, I finally got to play Quake on the PS1, but that's before I found a better version that doesn't rely on "substantial AI assistance"
items.excerpt: A homebrew Quake port for PS1 was built with heavy AI coding assistance — and a rival hand-written port runs better, sparking a small but pointed comparison in the demoscene-adjacent porting community.
items.why: A rare head-to-head where vibe-coded and hand-crafted versions of the same technical project ship side by side and can actually be compared.

items.title: I Played NBA 2K27 with NVIDIA's "Pixel-Accurate" DLSS 5, and It's a Truly Generational Visual Leap That Can Only Improve
items.excerpt: Hands-on with NBA 2K27 running DLSS 5 ahead of launch, testing Nvidia's claim that the neural rendering pass is pixel-accurate to the authored scene rather than hallucinated.
items.why: "Pixel-accurate" is the whole argument — if it holds, the neural pass is a renderer; if not, it is a style filter over someone else's art.

items.title: NVIDIA DLSS 5 Performance Unveiled: 5x Faster Than Original Demo, 50% Perf Penalty on Average
items.excerpt: Nvidia shares the first performance figures for RTX 50 GPUs running DLSS 5: five times faster than the March demo, but still roughly a 50% average frame-rate penalty, with more optimizations promised.
items.why: Concrete numbers let studios decide whether a neural render pass is a shippable target or a screenshot mode.

items.title: NVIDIA DLSS 5 Is The Biggest Leap In Rendering Since 3D Itself, Powered By Neural Technology
items.excerpt: DLSS 5 launches with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, replacing traditional lighting and material shading with a learned pass that Nvidia claims delivers lifelike results from the same authored geometry.
items.why: If lighting and materials become a learned pass, look-dev and material authoring change job description, not just tooling.

items.title: Nvidia DLSS 5 releases this week with NBA 2K27, so the AI yassification filter's busy beautifying basketballers early doors
items.excerpt: DLSS 5 arrives September 3rd with NBA 2K27 as its debut title, and early looks show the controversial genAI graphics tech visibly reworking player faces and materials.
items.why: The sharpest framing of the objection: a model deciding what characters look like after the artists signed off.

items.title: Nvidia tech behind PUBG's genAI team mates will let folks chat to creature-collecting RPG Aniimo's not-Pokemon next year
items.excerpt: Nvidia ACE, the tech behind PUBG's genAI team mates, will let players hold conversations with creatures in the Pokemon-esque RPG Aniimo from early 2027.
items.why: Conversational NPCs move from tech demo to a shipping creature-collector — a genre where character writing is the entire product.

items.title: Nvidia DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction, out now, ups shadow quality and more accurately illuminates trash bags
items.excerpt: Nvidia released DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction, an upgraded version of its path-tracing denoiser, available today with better shadow quality and more accurate indirect lighting.
items.why: The uncontroversial half of neural rendering: a learned denoiser that lets lighting artists ship path tracing at real budgets.

items.title: Dwarf Fortress Creator Calls Out One Of AI's Biggest Issues: The Bosses Who Force Us To Use It
items.excerpt: Tarn Adams argues the real problem with generative AI in game development isn't the tools but mandated adoption: 'Everyone I know, their bosses are slowly getting psychosis.'
items.why: Relocates the AI-in-craft argument from capability to mandate — the version of the debate most working designers actually live in.

items.title: Nvidia Confirms AI-Slop Filter DLSS 5 Will Cut Framerates In Half
items.excerpt: Nvidia's own figures confirm DLSS 5's neural rendering roughly halves frame rates, adding a performance argument to the aesthetic objections already aimed at the tech.
items.why: The consumer-side counterweight: a generative visual layer that costs both authored look and performance has a narrow case to make.

items.title: We're finally talking about AI, ft. David 'Rez' Graham and Luke Dicken
items.excerpt: Two veteran game AI practitioners discuss AI techniques in game development — and the conversation turns into one about the nature of work and where AI's inherent value in games actually sits.
items.why: Game AI specialists separating decades-old behavior AI from generative AI — the vocabulary distinction most coverage collapses.

items.title: No, the Humankind 2 announcement trailer wasn't made with gen-AI, despite it sharing a similar kind of look
items.excerpt: Amplitude clarifies that the Humankind 2 reveal trailer was human-made after viewers flagged it as looking AI-generated — a growing hazard for stylised art direction.
items.why: The false-positive problem is now an art-direction constraint: certain legitimate styles read as generated and studios have to defend them.
